# MLang Quick Guide
This page is a short “how do I start writing MLang?” guide.

For the full reference, see:
- [MLang Documentation Main Page](Home)
- [Language Syntax](Language-Syntax)
- [Stdlib Module API](Stdlib-Module-API)

## Hello World

```rust
fn main() -> i32 {
    println!("hello");
    return 0;
}
```

Notes:
- `main` usually returns [`i32`](Quick-Guide#types)
- plain `fn main() {}` is also accepted and defaults to `-> i32`

## Variables

```rust
fn main() -> i32 {
    let name: str8 = "mlang";
    var count: i32 = 3;
    count = count + 1;
    println!("{} {}", name, count);
    return 0;
}
```

- [`let`](Language-Syntax) is immutable
- [`var`](Language-Syntax) is mutable

## Common Types

```rust
let n: i32 = 42;
let ok: bool = true;
let ch: bit = 1;
let text: str8 = "hello";
let colored: str8 = "\x1b[38;2;164;255;82mhello\x1b[0m";
let utf16_text: str16 = String16::from(text);
let values: list<i32> = [1, 2, 3];
```

Common builtin/container types:
- [`i8`](Quick-Guide#types), [`i16`](Quick-Guide#types), [`i32`](Quick-Guide#types), [`i64`](Quick-Guide#types), [`u8`](Quick-Guide#types), [`u16`](Quick-Guide#types), [`u32`](Quick-Guide#types), [`u64`](Quick-Guide#types), [`f32`](Quick-Guide#types), [`f64`](Quick-Guide#types)
- [`bool`](Quick-Guide#types)
- [`bit`](Quick-Guide#types)
- [`str8`](Quick-Guide#types), [`str16`](Quick-Guide#types)
- [`list<T>`](Quick-Guide#types)
- [`Vec<T>`](Stdlib-Module-API#stdvec)
- [`span<T>`](Stdlib-Module-API#stdspan) / [`Span<T>`](Stdlib-Module-API#stdspan)
- [`Option<T>`](Quick-Guide#types)
- [`Result<T, E>`](Quick-Guide#types)

Integer type names use bit width, not byte width. For example, [`i8`](Quick-Guide#types) is an
8-bit signed integer (1 byte), while [`i64`](Quick-Guide#types) is a 64-bit signed integer (8 bytes).

| Type | Meaning | Range |
|---|---|---|
| [`i8`](Quick-Guide#types) | signed 8-bit integer | -128 to 127 |
| [`i16`](Quick-Guide#types) | signed 16-bit integer | -32768 to 32767 |
| [`i32`](Quick-Guide#types) | signed 32-bit integer | -2147483648 to 2147483647 |
| [`i64`](Quick-Guide#types) | signed 64-bit integer | -9223372036854775808 to 9223372036854775807 |
| [`u8`](Quick-Guide#types) | unsigned 8-bit integer | 0 to 255 |
| [`u16`](Quick-Guide#types) | unsigned 16-bit integer | 0 to 65535 |
| [`u32`](Quick-Guide#types) | unsigned 32-bit integer | 0 to 4294967295 |
| [`u64`](Quick-Guide#types) | unsigned 64-bit integer | 0 to 18446744073709551615 |

## Control Flow

```rust
if count > 10 {
    println!("large");
} else if count > 0 {
    println!("small");
} else {
    println!("zero");
}
```

```rust
switch count {
case 0: {
    println!("zero");
}
case 1: {
    println!("one");
}
default: {
    println!("many");
}
}
```

## Functions

```rust
fn add(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 {
    return a + b;
}
```

MLang also supports return-type inference for non-extern functions in many
cases. See [Language Syntax](Language-Syntax).

## Structs and Enums

```rust
struct Point {
    var x: i32;
    var y: i32;
}

enum Color {
    Red,
    Green,
    Blue,
}
```

```rust
let p = Point { x: 10, y: 20 };
println!("{} {}", p.x, p.y);
```

## Results and Match

```rust
fn divide(a: i32, b: i32) -> Result<i32, str8> {
    if b == 0 {
        return Err("divide by zero");
    }
    return Ok(a / b);
}

fn main() -> i32 {
    match divide(8, 2) {
    Ok(v) => {
        println!("value={}", v);
    }
    Err(msg) => {
        println!("error={}", msg);
    }
    }
    return 0;
}
```

## Exceptions

```rust
mod std::exceptions;

fn run() {
    throw Exception::new("ParseError", "bad token");
}

fn main() -> i32 {
    try {
        run();
    } catch e: Exception {
        println!("caught {}: {}", e.type_name, e.message);
    }
    return 0;
}
```

## C Interop

```rust
extern fn puts(text: str8) -> i32;

fn main() -> i32 {
    puts("hello from libc");
    return 0;
}
```

Use `extern fn` when calling C APIs or wrapped native libraries.

## Sizes and Static Assertions

```rust
let values: Span<i32> = [1, 2, 3];
static_assert!(size_of(values) == size_of(list<i32>));
static_assert!(size_of(array<i32, 6>) == 24);
println!("size={}", size_of(values));
```

## Testing

Mark functions with `#[test]` and run with `mlang --tests`:

```rust
mod std::testing;
use std::testing::*;

#[test]
fn test_addition() -> void {
    expect_eq_i32(4, 2 + 2);
}
```

```sh
mlang --tests path/to/file.mla            # one file
mlang --tests tests/                      # all suites in a directory
mlang --tests tests/ --filter "addition"  # filter by name
```

For tests that need shared setup, use a `#[fixture]` impl. Each `#[test]`
method runs against a fresh, zero-initialized instance:

```rust
struct DbFixture { var conn: i64; };

#[fixture]
impl DbFixture {
    fn setup(self: &mut Self) -> void { self.conn = 42; }
    fn teardown(self: &mut Self) -> void { self.conn = 0; }

    #[test]
    fn test_uses_setup(self: &mut Self) -> void {
        expect_eq_i64(42, self.conn);
    }
}
```

For mocks with cardinality and programmable return values, see the
EXPECT_CALL section in [Stdlib Module API](Stdlib-Module-API#stdtesting).
